nodes.name: Preparation of CoFe-LDH
nodes.procedure: CoFe-LDH was synthesized via a co-precipitation method. In brief, 40 ml solution A: Fe(NO3)3·6H2O (0.05 M) and Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.1 M) and 40 ml solution B: NaOH (0.75 M) and Na2CO3 (0.125 M) were firstly prepared. Solution A and B were added dropwisely at the same time into a beaker filled with 40 ml of deionized water. The pH value of the final suspension was adjusted to 8.5 under magnetic stirring, as monitored using a pH meter at room temperature (25 °C). The resulted suspension was aged for 12 h at 25 °C. Subsequently, the precipitate was collected by centrifugation, and washed 3 times using DI water, followed by ethanol wash for 3 times. The final precipitates were dried in a vacuum oven at 60 °C overnight.

nodes.name: Preparation of Ir/CoFe-LDH
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared CoFe-LDH (0.2 g) was added to 50 ml DI water under magnetic stirring to form a colloid suspension. Then, 10 ml freshly made aqueous IrCl3 solution (5 mg) containing 0.02 M NaOH was dropwisely added to the above CoFe-LDH colloid suspension. The suspension was stirred with simultaneous heating at 60 °C for 6 h. Afterwards, the precipitate was collected by centrifugation, washed by DI water and ethanol, each for 3 times. Then, the final precipitates were dried in a vacuum oven at 60 °C overnight.

nodes.name: Working Electrode Fabrication
nodes.procedure: 2 mg of the as-synthesized catalyst, 1 mg of carbon black, and 10 µl of Nafion solution were dispersed in ethanol (0.7 ml) and deionized water (0.7 ml) under ultrasonication for at least 1 h to form a homogeneous catalyst ink. The catalyst ink was drop-casted onto carbon fiber paper (1 cm x 1 cm, Toray, TGP-H-060) 50 µl each time with drying under an infrared lamp, followed by dropping another 50 µl ink until the catalyst mass-loading of the catalyst reached 2 mg/cm2.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns match the hexagonal-phase LDH (PDF#40-0215) for both the support and the Ir-loaded catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the as-prepared CoFe-LDH and Ir/CoFe-LDH display the same Bragg reflections in good agreement with the hexagonal-phase LDH (black line, PDF#40-0215, as shown in Fig. 1c)

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ DRIFTS of CO adsorption confirms atomic dispersion of Ir through the presence of symmetric and anti-symmetric vibrational modes of Ir gem-dicarbonyl at 2080 and 2010 cm-1; in contrast, Ircluster/CoFe-LDH exhibits linear binding peaks at 2046 cm-1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After adsorption of CO on Ir/CoFe-LDH, two bands (2080 and 2010 cm-1 can be clearly seen ... Ircluster /CoFe-LDH exhibits multiple overlapped IR peaks between 2000 and 2080 cm -1 ... strongest peak at 2046 cm -1 is assigned to the linear binding of CO on Ir clusters

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS identifies Ir-O (61.7 eV) and Ir-Cl (62.4 eV) species; Cl 2p peaks confirm Ir-Cl and Cl- on LDH. Shift in Co and Fe binding energies suggests strong electronic interaction between Ir and the support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ir 4f XPS spectrum showed two distinct peaks ... Ir 4f 7/2 at 61.7 eV and 62.4 eV were identified as the Ir-O and Ir-Cl ... Co and Fe have obvious shift of binding energy, indicating strong electronic interaction between single atomic Ir and CoFe-LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L3-edge XANES indicates the Ir valence state in Ir/CoFe-LDH is slightly higher than +4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ir L3-edge XANES spectrum (Fig. 1d) indicates that the valence state of Ir in Ir/CoFe-LDH is slightly higher than +4.
